items.title: Dario Defends Himself, Datacenter Panic, AI Doomer Trap, Senate Toss-Up
items.note: All-In episode 286, released August 21, 2026, in which Chamath and co-hosts react to Dario Amodei defending Anthropic against Gavin Baker's criticism, plus discussion of AI doom narratives and the Senate.

items.title: AI has literally zero to do with big company earnings growth
items.note: On X around August 20, 2026, Chamath argued Global 2000 earnings growth has almost nothing to do with AI spending, a claim widely covered days before Nvidia's Q3 earnings report.

items.title: Zuck knows great engineers want to join a space, search, or AI company, not an advertising company
items.note: Chamath posted on X around August 19, 2026 that Mark Zuckerberg avoids emphasizing Meta's ad business because top engineers prefer space, search, or AI focused companies.

items.title: Forgiving Yourself with Mary J. Blige
items.note: IMO episode with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson released August 19, 2026, in which Mary J. Blige discusses healing, self worth, and choosing a child free life at 55.

items.title: David Sacks accuses Anthropic's Dario Amodei of trying to create a 'DMV for AI'
items.note: Covers the public clash between venture capitalist David Sacks and Dario Amodei over Anthropic's push for AI safety regulation, which Sacks compared to a DMV style bureaucracy.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report that Anthropic plans to issue supervoting shares to CEO Dario Amodei and its other co-founders ahead of a planned IPO, since his ownership stake has fallen to roughly 2 percent.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report names Daniela Amodei among the seven Anthropic co-founders, including her brother Dario, set to receive supervoting shares ahead of the company's planned IPO.

items.title: Anthropic CEO says AI backlash is 'fundamentally a crisis of trust'
items.note: TechCrunch covers Amodei's mid-August public response to investor Gavin Baker, where he pushed back on the claim that his warnings have been disproportionately negative and framed the AI backlash as a crisis of trust.

items.title: You cannot create God and put him on a leash
items.note: Naval posted this one line warning about AI on X on August 15, 2026, prompting Elon Musk to reply that he hopes AI is nice to us.

items.title: Rio de Clarice: filme adapta cinco contos de Clarice Lispector
items.note: The film Rio de Clarice opened in Brazilian theaters on August 13, adapting five Lispector short stories through five Brazilian filmmakers, with a script co-written by her grand niece Nicole Allgranti and biographer Teresa Montero.

items.title: REG - Prosus NV Naspers Limited - Director/PDMR Shareholding
items.note: Regulatory disclosure dated August 12, 2026 covering Fabricio Bloisi's exercise and sale of Naspers and linked Prosus share options ahead of their August 2026 expiry.

items.title: 70 anos de Grande Sertão: Veredas: nova edição e biografia de Guimarães Rosa reforçam legado do autor
items.note: Article marking 70 years since Grande Sertao Veredas covers a new deluxe Companhia das Letras edition and the newly published biography of Guimaraes Rosa.

items.title: The Dollar's Dominance is Eroding
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights piece on finance professor Arvind Krishnamurthy's research on why investors are placing less value on the dollar's traditional safe haven status, noting a 6.5 percent drop against the euro during recent market turmoil.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto + Shiro Takatani: Ambient Kyoto, Tokyo
items.note: The Ambient Kyoto exhibition opens for the first time in Tokyo at Azabudai Hills Gallery from August 28 to October 25, featuring async immersion, an installation by Ryuichi Sakamoto and Shiro Takatani built around a 26.4 meter screen with new spatial sound design.

items.title: Megan Thee Stallion on Her Journey, Owning Her Power & What Act III Has In Store | IMO
items.note: IMO episode released August 12, 2026, in which Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson talk with Megan Thee Stallion about fame, grief, social media boundaries and her upcoming album.

items.title: Yvon Chouinard Was Destroying the Mountains He Loved. He Made 1 Painful Decision That Built the Patagonia Empire
items.note: Inc. piece published August 4, 2026 revisiting Chouinard's decision to abandon pitons, the environmental call that reshaped his business decades before sustainability became a buzzword.

items.title: World Premiere of Clarice Lispector's The Hour of the Star in Los Angeles
items.note: Brazilian actress Bruna Fachetti premiered a one-woman stage adaptation of Lispector's novella The Hour of the Star at The Broadwater in Los Angeles, running July 25 to August 1, 2026.

items.title: Open-model AI is good competition for Anthropic and OpenAI
items.note: Washington Post op-ed where Gurley argues Chinese open-weight models are healthy free-market competition, not a security threat to ban. It set off a week of open-source AI debate.

items.title: All-In podcast host Chamath Palihapitiya on the current state of AI
items.note: CNBC Squawk Box appearance on July 14 in his role as 8090 CEO, covering the AI capex boom. His line that 'you're starting to see a little bit of the wheels come off' AI spending was widely quoted.

items.title: Leonencio Nossa lança biografia de Guimarães Rosa durante Semana Rosiana em Cordisburgo
items.note: Journalist Leonencio Nossa launched a 736-page biography of Guimarães Rosa on July 10, 2026, during the Semana Rosiana in Cordisburgo, drawing on Itamaraty archives and nearly 2,000 of Rosa's letters.

items.title: 38ª Semana Rosiana celebra os 70 anos de Grande Sertão: Veredas e Corpo de Baile
items.note: Cordisburgo, Rosa's birthplace in Minas Gerais, hosted the 38th Semana Rosiana on July 5 to 11, 2026, marking 70 years since the 1956 publication of Grande Sertão: Veredas and Corpo de Baile.

items.title: Se Eu Fosse Eu, Clarices
items.note: Stage production by ATA built from three Lispector stories, O Ovo e a Galinha, Miss Algrave and Perdoando Deus, which returned to Rio for a run at the Centro Cultural da Justiça Federal from July 3 to 26, 2026.

items.title: Live in the Future
items.note: Naval podcast episode from July 2 with Garry Tan, Daniel Francis and Farbood Nivi, on riding AGI, AI anxiety, defending Taiwan and the 'California Empire'.

items.title: Noton to release posthumous Ryuichi Sakamoto LP 12 Conversations with Alva Noto
items.note: Noton announced 12 Conversations, a posthumous collaborative album by Sakamoto and Alva Noto recorded in late 2022, set for release on September 18, 2026.

items.title: Daniela Amodei Says Curiosity Is Underrated
items.note: Stanford GSB's View From The Top podcast episode, published June 29, 2026. She covers her path from English literature to Anthropic, why she left OpenAI, and the tension between safety and revenue.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto and Tin Drum: KAGAMI+
items.note: Japan premiere of the mixed-reality concert piece that captures Sakamoto's piano performance in three dimensions, running June 27 to October 12, 2026 at VS. in Umekita, Osaka. Currently on view.

items.title: Some U.S. Cities Solved Homelessness. The Rest Should Just Copy Them.
items.note: P3 Institute Substack post from June 23 arguing that a few cities have working homelessness playbooks and policy should copy what already works.

items.title: Leading for Tomorrow: Unlocking Human Potential in the Era of Continuous Change and Endless Possibility
items.note: New Wiley essay collection published June 22, 2026. Jennifer Aaker contributed a chapter, 'What Matters Now: Mortality, Meaning, and the Machine Age,' co-written with Sophie Hamilton.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time at Hamburger Bahnhof
items.note: Berlin's Hamburger Bahnhof announced the touring Sakamoto retrospective will open September 11, 2026 and run to May 23, 2027, his first major European retrospective.

items.title: Beth Goulart retoma peça sobre Clarice Lispector após mais de uma década fora de cartaz
items.note: Actress Beth Goulart brought her solo show Simplesmente Eu, Clarice Lispector back to Sao Paulo for the first time in 16 years, running from May 8 through June 28 at Teatro Moise Safra.

items.title: Vastlands: The Crossing
items.note: Alison Entrekin's long-awaited English translation of Grande Sertão: Veredas, a decade in the making, published in June 2026. The first new English version of Rosa's masterpiece since 1963, timed with the novel's 70th anniversary.
